name: Lazarus Synthetic Personhood Formal Witness Robe
description:
Lazarus produces this robe for the formal witnesses — physicians, legal advocates, and Lazarus representatives — who attend Synthetic Personhood hearings under the GLMZ Bioethics Tribunal framework. The robe is white synthetic silk with a pale blue panel at the left breast, the Tribunal's neutrality marker. It is deliberately simple: no corporate insignia beyond a small Lazarus rod-and-helix at the collar, no rank indicators, no chromatic thread. The message is that the wearer is present as a witness to a process, not as an advocate for any outcome. The fabric is easy to clean and resists the specific staining patterns of the Tribunal's ink-and-seal documentation process.

Lazarus's involvement in Synthetic Personhood hearings is commercially motivated — Synthetics with legal personhood can enter into medical contracts, purchase Lazarus services, and be covered under Ouroboros health policies. The robe's clinical simplicity is genuine in construction but not in context. Advocates who wear it know this. Some wear it anyway because the hearings require a witness and someone has to show up.
cultural_context: The white-and-blue Lazarus witness robe is recognizable to anyone who follows Synthetic rights cases. Activists argue that Lazarus's presence at these hearings — marked by the robe — legitimizes a process that remains fundamentally biased. Synthetics who have won personhood status sometimes express complicated gratitude toward the witnesses who wore it.
story_hooks: The character is asked to wear the robe as a witness for a Synthetic they know personally. The hearing goes badly. They keep the robe afterward and don't know why.

A gray-market version of the robe — without the Lazarus helix, just the blue panel — is being worn by unauthorized advocates who are disrupting hearings with unsanctioned testimony. The Tribunal wants them stopped. The character knows one of them.

A Synthetic who won personhood three years ago has preserved the robe worn by their primary witness. They want to return it — or give it to someone. The gesture means something that doesn't have a clean translation into legal language.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flowing, knee-length robe with clinical precision. High collar, straight lines, minimal drape. The left breast features a pale blue vertical panel—stark, unmissable, deliberately neutral. Silhouette reads formal and austere, suggesting medical authority without aggression.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso, designed to fit over layers or augmentation rigs without binding. Sleeves are three-quarter length, functional rather than decorative. Allows unrestricted arm movement for document handling and testimony gestures.
physical_description.primary_material: Synthetic silk—high-thread-count, pharmaceutical-grade. Soft to touch but with subtle rigidity for structure. Chosen for stain resistance and cleanability, not luxury.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost luminous surface with faint ribbed weave visible under direct light. No nap or pile—designed to shed ink, blood, biological residue without absorption. Feels clinical beneath fingertips.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pristine off-white (not pure white—warmer tone suggesting medical contexts). Pale blue panel at left breast is exact, institutional blue—the Tribunal's registered neutral marker. No other colors. No patterns.
physical_description.closures: Single long magnetic snap at the neckline discreetly marked with the Lazarus rod-and-helix symbol (small, chrome-plated, barely 8mm). No visible zippers or buttons. Friction-fit cuff seals at wrists allow easy removal of gloves or augmented limbs.
distinctive_features: Left-breast blue panel: intentional, required, unmissable
Lazarus rod-and-helix at collar: subtle, professional, unavoidable
Underarm reinforcement panels: designed to endure repeated hand-raising during testimony
Hidden document pockets along interior hem: stitched with reflective thread for low-light retrieval
Micro-weave grid visible only under magnification: pattern aids ink-seal adhesion, prevents document slippage
No rank indicators, no shoulder boards, no tier markers: deliberate institutional restraint
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 professional. Accessible to working-class advocates and mid-tier Lazarus staff, but costs Φ340-500 new. Signals institutional credibility without excessive wealth display.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this robe means you are present at a Synthetic Personhood hearing as a neutral witness. It signals medical/legal authority while attempting (imperfectly) to claim neutrality. In activist circles, it's controversial—seen by some as complicit in Lazarus's profiteering from Synthetic rights. Those who wear it often do so with acknowledged ambivalence. The robe carries the weight of that contradiction.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn robes show subtle ink staining around the pocket areas despite the stain-resistant weave. The blue panel may have pale watermarks from repeated exposure to Tribunal seal liquids. Edges remain crisp; fabric resists wrinkling. A well-maintained robe looks austere and competent. A worn one looks weathered by institutional use.
